description: CHART 13 - Slope chart (advanced idiom). The two main reasons Australians give for not buying (more) organic food that were asked in both 2022 and 2026: price or value, and trust or authenticity (Mobium Group Organic Consumer Research, in the Australian Organic Market Report). Why a slope chart: two points in time for a few categories; each line's slope shows whether a barrier grew, shrank or stayed the same, and its height shows how big it is (Kirk). It is a true slope graph (two parallel time axes joined by lines), not a dumbbell/dot plot. Barriers only asked in 2026 (availability, validation) have nothing to compare, so they are left out of the chart and mentioned in the text instead. Transforms: keep rows with a value; joinaggregate counts each barrier's years and the filter keeps barriers asked in both. Orange = the key fact (price), grey = trust. Faint gridlines at 0-100% make heights readable. The x and y encodings at the top are shared by all layers.

layer.description: Layer 1: thin vertical guide lines for the two years (the two parallel axes of the slope graph).
Layer 2: one line per barrier joining its 2022 and 2026 values.
Layer 3: a dot at every value, with a tooltip.
Layer 4: 2022 values written to the left of the left-hand dots.
Layer 5: 2026 labels to the right of the right-hand dots, with the barrier name and value.
